explicit_contract.requirement: python3 /app/pysed/sed.py ARGS behaves like GNU sed 4.9 with LC_ALL=C: same stdout bytes and exit status
explicit_contract.source_locator: instruction.md:the same standard output, byte for byte, and the same exit status

explicit_contract.requirement: -n -E -s, -e pieces joined by newlines, script as first non-option argument, files or stdin
POSIX leftmost-longest matching; tied group captures not checked

inference_families.inferred_model: a/i/c take one-line or backslash-newline text, the text runs to end of line (a ; is text), \\ gives one backslash, pieces may be split across -e, appended text flushes at end of cycle or when N/n reads
inference_families.reasoning_chain: manual 3.x a/i/c sections describe both forms, GNU extensions and -e splitting with worked examples
inference_families.competing_interpretation: ; ends the text like other commands; one-line i/c unsupported

inference_families.inferred_model: s flags g p N Ng I/i M/m, any delimiter, backslash-newline in replacement
inference_families.reasoning_chain: manual s command section lists every flag and spelling
inference_families.competing_interpretation: only uppercase I/M; M only changes anchors
inference_families.evidence_discriminator: sed.txt:700-715 states i/I, m/M and dot vs newline in M mode

inference_families.inferred_model: GNU BRE/ERE with POSIX leftmost-longest (instruction), literal ^/$ off anchor position in BRE, leading * literal in a group, inclusive ranges, leading - literal, C-locale equivalence class = the character, back-references also case-folded under I
inference_families.reasoning_chain: chapter 5 tables and bracket section; instruction pins leftmost-longest and [=c=]
inference_families.competing_interpretation: Python re leftmost-first; ERE/BRE operator confusion

inference_families.inferred_model: \L \U end each other or at \E; \l \u apply to the next character even across an empty group
inference_families.competing_interpretation: one-char conversion consumed by an empty group

inference_families.inferred_model: line, $, first~step, /re/ and \cREc with I/M, ranges incl. addr1,+N addr1,~N (next multiple strictly after addr1) and 0,/re/
inference_families.competing_interpretation: addr1,~N ends at addr1 when it is a multiple; /x/id read as a modifier

inference_families.inferred_model: pattern/hold space, n N D P at end of input, t/T flag reset by a read or a taken branch (kept across D), q/Q codes, =, z, y with section 5.8 escapes
inference_families.reasoning_chain: manual command descriptions plus instruction clause for y escapes
inference_families.competing_interpretation: t flag sticky; D clears it; y lists raw
inference_families.evidence_discriminator: sed.txt:2678-2686 flag definition; instruction.md:6 y clause

inference_families.inferred_model: several files as one stream, -s per-file numbering and $, ranges not spanning files, empty file, missing file exit 2, - is stdin
inference_families.competing_interpretation: empty file ends input; - opened literally

inference_families.inferred_model: l escapes (C escapes, octal otherwise), at most N-1 escaped characters per output line before \ or $, default 70, l 0 never wraps
inference_families.reasoning_chain: instruction pins the wrap rule; manual shows escapes
inference_families.competing_interpretation: N characters before the backslash; never wrap by default

inference_families.inferred_model: #n first two characters, comments to end of line (; inside is comment), leading whitespace, options, -e joined by newlines, script as first non-option argument
inference_families.competing_interpretation: #n needs a newline; ; ends a comment

oracle_alignment.equivalence_notes: Expected output is GNU sed 4.9's own stdout and exit status at test time; byte-exact stdout is the domain requirement (a drop-in sed), so no alternative representation exists. Cases whose result depends on behaviour the manual leaves open were removed by alternative-reading variants.
